topic.title: Closing a Review Task
topic.shortdesc: Task owners close a review task to stop reviewers from making changes while feedback is addressed or prepared for integration.

body.p: A task owner can close a review task to pause reviewer editing and reserve time to address feedback before integration. To do this, open the task and click Close review in the review task header.

Closing a task changes its state to Review closed and locks the task for reviewers. Task owners can still work in the task. The individual review statuses remain visible after the task is closed. If more review is needed, a task owner can click Reopen review to make the task editable for reviewers again and reset the review statuses for the new review cycle.

Closing a task is not the same as a reviewer using Finalize my review. Finalizing only tells task owners that a reviewer finished their part of the review and changes that reviewer's individual review status to Finalized. It does not lock the task or change the task state. Closing a task is also different from deleting a task, which permanently removes it.

For tasks created outside a project, after a task owner integrates the changes into the source content, they can click Mark as integrated in the review task header. This archives the task, removes it from the reviewers task list, and makes it uneditable. Task owners can view their integrated tasks by opening the My Review Tasks page, going to the Owned By Me tab, and clicking Show integrated review tasks. To regain access to an integrated task, use Mark as not integrated.
